Company

An organization built around systems, not features.

Oblivion is a small independent studio with a human-plus-AI development model. It works across software engineering, AI-assisted development, agent systems, data and intelligence tooling, and game technology.

01

Applied research

We treat research as production infrastructure — every model, method, and dataset is versioned, reviewed, and accountable to a real system.

02

Systems engineering

Software is built to be operated for years, not demoed once. Reliability, observability, and clear failure modes are first-class requirements.

03

Disciplined design

Interfaces are built for people making consequential decisions under time pressure — clarity and information density over decoration.

ANGRA

Human direction, AI-agent execution.

ANGRA is Oblivion's model collaboration and integration bridge, built around local model environments such as LM Studio and Bionic. It is not a foundation model. The layers below describe the organizational design of about 100 agent roles; they are roles on paper, not 100 processes running continuously, and live agent execution is not part of this public site. Platform

Infrastructure philosophy

The platform is designed so that every privileged surface — files, models, users, and administration — sits behind the same set of architectural guarantees.

Zero trust

No request is trusted by network location alone. Every call to a privileged interface is authenticated and authorized independently, on every request.

Defense in depth

Security is layered — network, gateway, application, and data — so that no single control failure exposes the system.

Least privilege

Sessions and services are granted the minimum access required for their function, scoped by role and by object.

Secure by default, fail closed

Unclear or failed authorization decisions deny access rather than falling back to an open state.

CDN Edge delivery & caching
WAF / DDoS protection Perimeter defense
Reverse proxy / API gateway Routing & rate limiting
Identity & authorization layer WebAuthn, MFA, session policy
Application layer Service logic
Data & object storage Encrypted at rest
Audit & monitoring Full request & access trail
Security & Trust

What "secure" means here, stated plainly.

This page states the principles Oblivion designs against. It is not a claim that any system is unhackable, and nothing here is "military-grade" — that phrase gets used without evidence often enough that we'd rather just describe the actual practices.

Secure development

Code review, dependency review, and threat modeling are part of how a system ships, not a step added afterward. This file's own rendering layer is an example: everything dynamic is escaped through OblivionSecurity.esc(), and no dynamic script injection, eval(), or unsanitized HTML construction is used anywhere in it.

Auditability

Privileged actions are logged with enough context to reconstruct what happened and why — not just that something happened. The Control Center's audit log demonstrates the shape of this; production logging ships to a backend audit service rather than living in the browser.

Data handling

Data is classified, access is scoped to what a given session actually needs, and storage and transport are encrypted. What a system collects is bounded by what it needs to do its job.

Incident response

Systems are built assuming something will eventually go wrong: clear ownership, a defined escalation path, and postmortems that change the system rather than just closing a ticket.

Responsible disclosure

If you find a genuine security issue in something Oblivion operates, report it through the security disclosures link in the footer rather than public channels, and allow time to investigate and fix it before any public discussion.

For the infrastructure layers this maps onto in production, see Platform.

Scope & limitations

What this site is, and what it is not.

Oblivion publishes this as a static public site on GitHub Pages. We list the boundaries here so the work can be judged on what actually exists.

  • Public website. Static content. There is no server, database or account system behind it.
  • Demonstrations. Control Center, search and the ANGRA analysis are public demos. The Control Center gate is client-side and is not authentication; real access control would need a server-side backend, which does not exist yet.
  • Agent roles. The ~100 agents are a designed role model. They are not 100 autonomous agents running in production.
  • Oblivion Intelligence. Local retrieval over a built-in index. It is not a hosted language model, and no API key is stored or required.
  • Security headers. GitHub Pages cannot set custom response headers, so the Content-Security-Policy is delivered through a meta tag. That cannot enforce frame-ancestors or HSTS. Those need a header-capable host.
  • External services. Google Drive, two folders (only after you press Connect Google in Control Center, or when a read-only API key is configured), GitHub API (project list), a public RSS-to-JSON service as fallback for Medium writing, and a Python runtime from jsDelivr only when you press the ANGRA analysis button. Each has a fallback and the site works without them.
Maintainer kit: Medium sync files (7)

These files run in the GitHub repository, not in the browser. Download the zip, extract it into the repository root (paths are kept), and follow MEDIUM-SYNC.md. Nothing here executes on this page.

  • scripts/sync_medium.pyRSS fetch, validation, persistent archive
  • tests/test_sync_medium.pyAdversarial parser and failure tests (18)
  • .github/workflows/sync-medium.ymlHourly + manual workflow, no third-party actions
  • data/medium-seed.jsonOptional manual backfill template
  • sitemap.xmlSitemap for the project URL
  • robots.txtCrawler hints (informational on a project path)
  • MEDIUM-SYNC.mdSetup steps and limits

    Control Center

    This is a demonstration access gate for the privileged operations surface. It illustrates the intended interaction pattern only — see the note below for the real authentication architecture.

    Maintainer: protect this gate

    Type your three access values above, then press the button. Only salted PBKDF2-SHA-256 hashes (600,000 rounds) are produced, in this browser; the values are not stored or sent anywhere. Paste the result into <script id="ob-gate-config"> in index.html. The gate then verifies against the hashes instead of accepting any input.

    Demonstration only — this client-side gate is not production security. The real system is designed to authenticate with WebAuthn / passkeys and server-verified MFA, issue short-lived rotating sessions, and authorize every privileged request independently. Any three values will pass this demo.
